summary: Order submit failures (~31% error rate, 504s) are caused by degradation of the external exchange partner API (api.exchange-partner.example), surfaced through exchange-gateway. exchange-gateway shows upstream connect timeouts and 503s from exchange-api starting 11:01, driving 40-48% upstream error rate and ~9s upstream latency. order-service merely propagates these as "exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout". The onset aligns with exchange-gateway's upstream failures, NOT with the order-service v2.15.2 deploy (10:48) — and critically the deploy was already rolled back at 11:16:38 yet errors continue unchanged through 12:58. order-service CPU/memory/db-pool are flat with zero restarts, ruling out resource exhaustion; pricing-engine is healthy, ruling out the config change at 09:20. Root cause: dependency_failure at the external exchange provider.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange provider degradation (dependency_failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange partner API (api.exchange-partner.example, fronted by exchange-api) began timing out and returning 503s at ~11:01. exchange-gateway's upstream calls hit connect timeouts (~9s upstream latency) and its circuit breaker opened, propagating 504s to order-service, which reports ~31% order submit failures.

causal_chain.claim: External exchange partner degrades; api.exchange-partner.example connect timeouts and 503s appear at 11:01
exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate rises to ~46% and upstream_latency to ~9s; circuit breaker opens
order-service order submit error_rate reaches ~31% and p99 ~5.3s

assumptions: exchange-api is a thin proxy to the external partner and the fault is on the partner side, not on our edge

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 release introduced the faults
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The order-service v2.15.2 deploy (idempotency keys in order submit) at 10:48 caused the 30% submit failure rate.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Deploy was rolled back at 11:16:38 but errors continued unchanged through 12:58; the error signature ('exchange-gateway call failed: 504') points to a downstream failure, not order-service code; exchange-gateway shows an independent upstream failure starting 11:01 with no deploy of its own.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine cache TTL config change caused the failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The cfg-2290 cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 change at 09:20 degraded pricing and cascaded to orders.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine error_rate is flat ~0.2% and the change predates onset by 1h40m; order errors are all exchange-gateway 504s, unrelated to pricing.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service resource exhaustion (CPU/memory/DB pool)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service exhausted CPU, memory or DB connections, causing latency and failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU ~40%, db_pool ~14 and request_rate flat throughout; no restarts. Slow latency is explained by the downstream 504 wait.

facts.statement: order-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~31% at the 11:00 bucket and remained elevated through 12:45.
order-service latency_p99 rose from ~150ms to ~5300ms at 11:00.
All order-service ERROR logs are 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'.
exchange-gateway logged upstream connect timeouts to api.exchange-partner.example and 503s from exchange-api starting 11:01:25.
exchange-gateway error_rate ~44%, upstream_error_rate ~46%, upstream_latency ~9.2s during the incident.
exchange-gateway circuit breaker opened for exchange-api at 11:03:26.
order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) was deployed 10:48 and rolled back at 11:16.
Rollback completed at 11:16:38 but errors continued unchanged through 12:58.
order-service CPU (~40%), db_pool (~14) and request_rate (~230/s) were flat during the incident.
exchange-gateway had zero restarts and flat CPU (~30%).
Only config change was pricing-engine cache TTL 5->4 at 09:20.
exchange-api is an external vendor node without telemetry.
No exchange-gateway deployments in the window.
api-gateway logged no WARN/ERROR entries during the incident.

assumptions: exchange-api (external vendor node without telemetry) is a proxy for api.exchange-partner.example, so the outage is on the partner side rather than in our own edge.
No other relevant change occurred outside the queried windows.

timeline.event: exchange-gateway first upstream connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example
exchange-gateway circuit breaker opens for exchange-api
order-service rollback of dep-5333 complete; errors persist unchanged

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating the order-service rollback as the fix; engage the exchange partner / vendor to restore api.exchange-partner.example, and fail over to a secondary exchange route if available.
recommended_actions.rationale: Fault originates at the external provider; rollback did not help and errors persist.

recommended_actions.action: Verify whether exchange-api is a proxy to the partner vs. our own component, and check its health/credentials to confirm the fault boundary.
recommended_actions.rationale: exchange-api has no telemetry, so the exact boundary between our gateway and the partner is unconfirmed.

recommended_actions.action: Tune exchange-gateway circuit breaker / add fast-fail and secondary-route failover so external partition degrades gracefully instead of 30% order failures.
recommended_actions.rationale: Circuit breaker opened but requests still propagated 504s to orders for ~2h.

recommended_actions.action: Add monitoring/telemetry on exchange-api and partner connectivity to detect external degradation at onset.
recommended_actions.rationale: The external node has no telemetry, delaying detection.

data_gaps: exchange-api/external provider has no telemetry (has_telemetry false), so the partner-side health is inferred only from exchange-gateway logs.
exchange-gateway request_rate query timed out (tc-019), so its own request volume during the incident is unconfirmed.
No vendor status page or partner-side incident record was available to independently confirm the external outage.
